transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess I’m here because I don’t really feel like myself anymore. I used to be pretty active—hiking, coaching, playing guitar, all that. I mean, I still have my old guitar sitting there, and sometimes I look at it and think I should pick it up, but then I don’t.

And people call or text, and I just… don’t call them back. It’s not even that I’m mad at anybody. I just sit in my rental sometimes for hours, knowing there are things I’m supposed to do, and I can’t get myself to start. It’s weird, because I used to be the guy who got things done. At work, in protective service, you can’t just sit around, you know? But now even small stuff feels like… too much.
Do memories of something traumatic ever pop into your mind when you don’t want them to?

I don’t know… traumatic like, something specific? I mean, I’ve had rough days on the job, everybody has, but I don’t really get some memory jumping out at me like that, not that I’ve noticed.

Sometimes my mind goes places I didn’t ask it to, but it’s not like one clear event replaying. It’s more like I start thinking about one thing and then I’m thinking about the truck I used to drive, or a call I forgot to return, or whether the neighbor’s dog is barking more than usual… sorry, that’s not really what you asked. So, no, I don’t think so.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Down… yeah, I don’t know. Maybe. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m walking around crying or anything. It’s more like things feel kind of flat, like the day starts and then I look up and it’s afternoon and I haven’t really done much.

But depressed… I don’t know if that’s the word. My sister uses that word for everything, like if her football team loses she says she’s depressed, which always kind of annoyed me because words should mean something. Sorry—yeah, I guess I haven’t felt good lately. Not like myself.
Was there a specific stressful event in your life before you started feeling this way?

I mean… yeah, kind of. It wasn’t like one single thing happened on a Tuesday or whatever. It’s more that after the divorce, when I moved into that smaller rental place, things started… slipping.

That was about a year and two months ago, I think. Funny, I remember because the landlord had this weird rule about trash bins being out by exactly 6 a.m., and I thought, who is watching trash bins that closely? But anyway—yeah, since moving there after the divorce, that’s when it feels like things started unraveling.
For most of the day, nearly every day, have you been feeling sad or down?

Most of the day… I’m not sure how to measure that, exactly. Like, I wake up and I don’t always think “I’m sad,” it’s more like I’m just there, you know? Moving slow.

Some days it’s worse, some days I get distracted by things—mail piling up, noise outside, whether I left something on—and then I realize I haven’t really felt okay for a while. But “nearly every day,” I don’t know. I guess a lot of days. I wouldn’t want to say it wrong.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hiking, coaching, or playing guitar?

Yeah… yeah, I have. I used to hike a lot, and I coached, and I’d mess around on guitar at night. Now I just… don’t. It’s not like I decided to quit, exactly. It’s more like I look at the guitar and it might as well be a piece of furniture.

And the coaching thing—there was this kid once who couldn’t remember to keep his elbows in, and I spent weeks telling him, elbows, elbows, elbows… funny what sticks in your head. But now if someone asks me to help out or calls, I don’t call back. I mean to. I’ll see the message and think, okay, in a minute.

Mostly I just don’t feel like myself anymore. Some days I sit in that little rental for hours, knowing there are things I should do, even simple things, but I can’t get myself started.
Before this past year, have you ever gone through another period in your life when you felt this same way?

I don’t know… not really like this, I don’t think. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before. Everybody has, right? Work stress, bad nights, arguments, that kind of thing.

There was a time years ago when I was working a lot of overtime and I remember eating mostly gas station sandwiches—those ones in the triangle plastic, always too cold in the middle—and I felt worn down, but that’s not the same thing, I don’t think.

So… before this past year, I can’t really point to another time that felt the same. Not in this same way.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself, like you're observing yourself from the outside or things around you don’t feel real?

I don’t know… I don’t think so. Not like I’m floating over myself or watching a movie or anything.

Sometimes things feel kind of strange, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. Like if I’m sitting in the room too long and the light changes, everything gets… I don’t know, flat maybe? But then I start thinking about whether I paid the electric bill, and there was this envelope I put somewhere—unless I threw it out with the grocery bags, because I do that sometimes, I’ll set something down and it just disappears.

So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling outside my body, if that’s the question.
Before these changes started, did you have a head injury, stroke, seizure, or another major medical illness?

Not that I can think of… I mean, I’ve bumped my head before, everybody has, especially with work and just… life, you know. One time I remember hitting my forehead on the corner of a cabinet in this old break room, and the coffee machine there made this clicking sound all day, like it was trying to talk but couldn’t get the words out.

But, uh… no, I don’t think there was some big thing like that before all this started. No stroke or seizure that I know of. Major illness… I don’t think so. I mean, unless I’m forgetting something, but nothing that anybody told me was serious.
Do you feel hopeless?

Hopeless… I don’t know. That’s a big word, isn’t it? Like when people say it they mean there’s nothing left, and I don’t know if I’d say it like that.

Some days I wake up and it feels like… like everything’s already stacked up before I even get my shoes on. And then I’ll get stuck thinking about stupid things, like the lock on the back door or whether the neighbor’s trash cans were out on the wrong day, and somehow the whole morning is gone.

So, hopeless? Maybe sometimes I feel close to that. I don’t know how to measure it. I’m still here, I’m still talking to you, so I guess part of me thinks there’s a point to it. But it’s hard to hold onto sometimes.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

I don’t know… I mean, I’ve had days where I think, “What’s the point of all this?” but then that could mean a lot of things, right? Like when the alarm goes off and the whole day feels like it’s already waiting to crush you.

But “life isn’t worth living”… I don’t know if I’ve put it that exact way. Sometimes I get tired, really tired, and I just sit there staring at something dumb, like the pattern on the wall or the little dust on the TV stand, and it feels like everything is too much. Then I remember I was supposed to call somebody back, or there’s laundry still in the machine, and I get pulled into that.

So… I’m not sure. I guess sometimes it feels close to that, but I don’t know.
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself?

I… I don’t know. I don’t think I’m sitting here with a plan like that, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like things get loud in my head and I get worn down, and then I start thinking too much.

Killing myself… that sounds so direct. I haven’t been, um… I don’t want to say the wrong thing. Sometimes I just want everything to stop for a while, like when you’re on a long shift and the radio keeps crackling and nobody answers right, and you’re just standing there waiting for something to happen. But that’s not the same, maybe.

So… I’m not sure how to answer. I don’t think I’m trying to kill myself.
Have you wished you could go to sleep and not wake up?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve thought about sleep like that, but I don’t know if I mean not wake up. Sleep is strange anyway, because sometimes you go down and it feels like five minutes, and other times you wake up and the whole room feels different, like you missed something important.

There are nights where I just want to be gone from the day, you know? Like shut everything off. But “not wake up” is… I don’t know. That sounds heavier than what I can really say. I haven’t got a clean answer.

I guess sometimes I wish I could sleep for a long time and not have to deal with anything for a while. Whether that means not waking up… I’m not sure.
Did these problems start only after the divorce?

Not only after the divorce exactly… I mean, the divorce was part of it, but it was more when I moved into that smaller rental afterward. That place just—everything felt squeezed in, like the walls were closer, and the heat made this ticking sound at night that I kept noticing.

That was about… a year and two months ago, I think. Since then things have just been kind of unraveling. The divorce was the start of the whole change, but the problems really started getting worse after I was living there.
Is the divorce fully over now?

I’m not really sure what counts as fully over. I mean, papers and all that… there were papers, and phone calls, and those envelopes that make your stomach drop before you even open them.

I don’t live with her anymore, if that’s what you mean. It feels over in the house, like the rooms know it. But “fully” is a funny word, because things keep following you around after they’re supposed to be finished. Like when a call is cleared but you still hear it in your head driving back.

So… I think it’s over, mostly. I’m not sure about the exact official part.
Have these symptoms continued for more than six months after the divorce was over?

Yeah… I mean, if we’re counting from when it was over-over, I get mixed up with that. But the way I remember it, things started really coming apart when I moved into that smaller rental after the divorce.

That was about a year and two months ago. The place was cramped, and I remember the light coming through the blinds wrong in the mornings—anyway, since then it’s been going on. So… yes, more than six months, I think.
Have you noticed any new problems with your memory?

Memory… I don’t know. I mean, everybody forgets things, right? Like where you put your keys, or you walk into a room and forget why—my dad used to do that and then blame the dog, even when we didn’t have a dog anymore.

I haven’t really been keeping track of it like that. I can’t say I’ve noticed some big new memory problem. Sometimes everything just feels crowded in my head, but… I don’t know if that’s memory or just too much going on.
Nearly every day, have you been feeling tired or low on energy?

Yeah… most days, yeah. It’s not just sleepy-tired, though. It’s more like I don’t have the push in me.

I used to hike, and I coached, and I’d play guitar sometimes—badly, but still—and now I don’t really do any of it. I’ll see the guitar sitting there and think, okay, just pick it up, it’s right there, and then somehow an hour’s gone by. Same with calling people back. The phone feels heavy, which sounds stupid because it’s not heavy.

Some days I just sit in that small rental for hours, knowing there are things I should do, but I can’t get myself started. So… yeah. Low energy, nearly every day, I guess.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Sleep… I don’t know. I mean, I go to bed, but it’s not like flipping a switch, you know?

Some nights I’m just lying there thinking about the room, the pipes making noise, or whether I left something out, and then I start thinking about work schedules from years ago—there was this one night shift where the vending machine ate my dollar and everybody acted like that was the funniest thing in the world.

But trouble sleeping… I guess I haven’t really measured it. I don’t wake up and write it down or anything. It feels uneven. Some nights are worse than others.
Have you been diagnosed with any thyroid problem?

Thyroid… I don’t think so. Nobody’s told me that, not that I remember.

I’ve had regular doctor visits here and there, but they talk fast sometimes, and there’s always forms, insurance stuff, sitting under those buzzing lights in the waiting room… makes it hard to keep track. But no, I don’t have some thyroid diagnosis that I know of.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I’ve thought about sleep like that, but I don’t know if I mean not wake up. Sleep is strange anyway, because sometimes you go down and it feels like five minutes, and other times you wake up and the whole room feels different, like you missed something important.

There are nights where I just want to be gone from the day, you know? Like shut everything off. But “not wake up” is… I don’t know. That sounds heavier than what I can really say. I haven’t got a clean answer.

I guess sometimes I wish I could sleep for a long time and not have to deal with anything for a while. Whether that means not waking up… I’m not sure.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the symptoms began as a maladaptive response to an identifiable stressor and persisted beyond the usual window for adjustment disorder, helping distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder.

patient.answer:
Not only after the divorce exactly… I mean, the divorce was part of it, but it was more when I moved into that smaller rental afterward. That place just—everything felt squeezed in, like the walls were closer, and the heat made this ticking sound at night that I kept noticing.

That was about… a year and two months ago, I think. Since then things have just been kind of unraveling. The divorce was the start of the whole change, but the problems really started getting worse after I was living there.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms have persisted beyond 6 months after the stressor ended, which would help distinguish major depressive disorder from an adjustment disorder related to the divorce/move.
doctor.question: Is the divorce fully over now?

target_item.reason: The question asks about current divorce/legal relationship status, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure what counts as fully over. I mean, papers and all that… there were papers, and phone calls, and those envelopes that make your stomach drop before you even open them.

I don’t live with her anymore, if that’s what you mean. It feels over in the house, like the rooms know it. But “fully” is a funny word, because things keep following you around after they’re supposed to be finished. Like when a call is cleared but you still hear it in your head driving back.

So… I think it’s over, mostly. I’m not sure about the exact official part.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, if we’re counting from when it was over-over, I get mixed up with that. But the way I remember it, things started really coming apart when I moved into that smaller rental after the divorce.

That was about a year and two months ago. The place was cramped, and I remember the light coming through the blinds wrong in the mornings—anyway, since then it’s been going on. So… yes, more than six months, I think.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms are due to a general medical condition by screening for a clear neurological sign, which best distinguishes F06.3 from primary depression or adjustment disorder at this point.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any new problems with your memory?

target_item.reason: The question asks about memory problems, which are not covered by any listed symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Memory… I don’t know. I mean, everybody forgets things, right? Like where you put your keys, or you walk into a room and forget why—my dad used to do that and then blame the dog, even when we didn’t have a dog anymore.

I haven’t really been keeping track of it like that. I can’t say I’ve noticed some big new memory problem. Sometimes everything just feels crowded in my head, but… I don’t know if that’s memory or just too much going on.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether a core major depressive symptom is present nearly every day to distinguish major depressive disorder from an adjustment-related or mood-due-to-medical condition.
doctor.question: Nearly every day, have you been feeling tired or low on energy?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore—I stopped hiking, coaching, playing guitar, and calling people back, and some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things to do but I can't make myself start.
target_item.reason: The question is about persistent low energy, which is most closely reflected in diminished motivation and reduced activity in the negative symptoms profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… most days, yeah. It’s not just sleepy-tired, though. It’s more like I don’t have the push in me.

I used to hike, and I coached, and I’d play guitar sometimes—badly, but still—and now I don’t really do any of it. I’ll see the guitar sitting there and think, okay, just pick it up, it’s right there, and then somehow an hour’s gone by. Same with calling people back. The phone feels heavy, which sounds stupid because it’s not heavy.

Some days I just sit in that small rental for hours, knowing there are things I should do, but I can’t get myself started. So… yeah. Low energy, nearly every day, I guess.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive symptoms are better explained by a primary mood disorder versus a stress-related adjustment reaction by assessing a core major depressive symptom not yet established clearly.

patient.answer:
Sleep… I don’t know. I mean, I go to bed, but it’s not like flipping a switch, you know?

Some nights I’m just lying there thinking about the room, the pipes making noise, or whether I left something out, and then I start thinking about work schedules from years ago—there was this one night shift where the vending machine ate my dollar and everybody acted like that was the funniest thing in the world.

But trouble sleeping… I guess I haven’t really measured it. I don’t wake up and write it down or anything. It feels uneven. Some nights are worse than others.

patient.answer:
Thyroid… I don’t think so. Nobody’s told me that, not that I remember.

I’ve had regular doctor visits here and there, but they talk fast sometimes, and there’s always forms, insurance stuff, sitting under those buzzing lights in the waiting room… makes it hard to keep track. But no, I don’t have some thyroid diagnosis that I know of.
